title: ESP1 — Equilateral Small Polygons: First-Order Optimisation and Rigidity
description:
Formerly named Chiquipoli (release 1.3.1).

ESP1 is a computational tool for verifying sufficient conditions for strict local maximality of perimeter among equilateral small polygons. Based on realised diameter graphs, it combines exact algebra, validated interval arithmetic, positive active diameter multipliers and infinitesimal rigidity to establish local maximality modulo orientation-preserving Euclidean motions. A complementary Lean 4 formalisation is also provided.

As principal applications, ESP1 rigorously verifies strict local maximality for the Bingane–Audet polygons A16, A32 and A64, and for the configurations Z32 and Z64 reconstructed from their published descriptions. For n = 32, 64, the polygons Zn have strictly larger perimeters than An, demonstrating the coexistence of distinct strict local maximisers with different perimeters.

The software accompanies the article First Order Geometry of Equilateral Small Polygons by J. Ayala Hoffmann and T. Ayala Coppola.

What this archive is. Release 1.4.0 contains the certified sources (src/, pipeline/, test/, cases/, lean/), the run records (results/, logs/) and the documentation. The records in results/ were produced by make check-all (13 of 13 stages passed) from the Git commit named in the git_commit field of every record, with a clean working tree. This release commit differs from that commit only in results/, logs/ and the metadata files CITATION.cff, .zenodo.json and CHANGELOG.md; every source file whose SHA-256 is recorded is byte-identical.

Toolchain. Julia 1.12.6 with IntervalArithmetic.jl 0.22.36 (256-bit BigFloat intervals); Lean 4 toolchain leanprover/lean4:v4.33.0-rc1 with Mathlib revision ae0d973d69b779efa724095bd41793b8cf233831 (pinned in lean/lean-toolchain and lean/lake-manifest.json).

What it does not establish. Global optimality; that Z32 and Z64 are the polygons of Bingane and Audet (they are rebuilt from the description in their Propositions 1 and 2); the fidelity of the transcription of the OPTIGON constructor beyond the checks documented in the article.
